question: Should gateway restart attribution land as this PR's separate bounded `gateway_restart_audit` table, or should it be rebased and reshaped around current main's generic `audit_events` ledger before merge?
rationale: Current main gained a generic metadata-only audit ledger after this PR head, while this PR adds a separate restart-specific durable table and stores security-sensitive operational metadata; automation cannot choose that product/security boundary for maintainers.

options.title: Rebase and decide audit boundary
options.body: Resolve the current-main conflicts, then either wire restart events into the canonical audit direction or document why a separate restart table is the accepted boundary.

options.title: Accept the separate restart table
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept the new fixed-retention restart table as a separate operator-forensics store despite the generic audit ledger existing on main.

options.title: Pause for audit-ledger integration
options.body: If restart records should be part of the broader audit ledger, pause this PR until the generic event model supports restart events cleanly.

recommendation.title: Rebase and decide audit boundary
recommendation.body: Resolve the current-main conflicts, then either wire restart events into the canonical audit direction or document why a separate restart table is the accepted boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans restart observability, shared SQLite state, and the current audit-ledger product boundary where steipete has the strongest history signal.
